title: findings-cluster@2
description: Successor to findings-cluster@1, a byte-identity-forced re-registration: two field descriptions cited a past issue id in place as a lookup key, and the engine refuses an in-place edit to a frozen registration. Otherwise unchanged. The SYNTHESIZE document — declared on synthesize steps ONLY: never on judges (findings@6 owns that boundary) and never on reconcile (findings@5 owns the aggregate's carry-through, whose declared severity order the ordered thresholds compile from). Historically synthesize declared no `payload` because every findings@N put a property-level scalar `enum` on `severity`, which refuses the multi-member cluster shape the builtin `aggregate` reads — its `clusterMembers` takes member severities from the `severity` field itself, scalar-or-array (06 §2). The engine compiles full JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (schema.go), so this document writes that input contract down as an anyOf instead of leaving the seam unvalidated. What unvalidated cost, measured across 42 runs: the member-linkage key drifted into four spellings (`members`, `cluster_members`, `member_ids`, `member_findings`), and 23% of elements legitimately carried array severities nothing checked. This document standardizes `member_ids` as the ONE linkage key. No `ordered_enum` anywhere: no threshold reads this document, and the reconcile step's findings@5 keeps the declared order thresholds compile from.

id.description: Stable identifier for the cluster, unique within the payload. Required: the standing-set rules key re-occurrence and disposition on it, and this document is never declared on the aggregate step, so the V30 concern that keeps `id` optional on the cluster carry-through documents does not apply.

title.description: The defect stated once, in the synthesizer's own words.

severity.description: Scalar-or-array, the aggregate's INPUT contract (06 §2): a multi-member cluster carries the array of its members' severities in arrival order, and a single-member cluster — including a standing finding carried forward from an earlier round at the scalar the previous aggregate reduced it to — carries the scalar. Values are 02 §6's five: info, low, medium, high, blocker. Deliberately NOT `ordered_enum`: the order thresholds compare on is declared by findings@5 on the reconcile step, and declaring a second order here would be a second source of truth.

member_ids.description: The `id`s of the judge findings this cluster merges, in the same arrival order as an array `severity`'s values. THE one member-linkage key: `members` is the aggregate's OUTPUT record and the pre-schema variants (`cluster_members`, `member_findings`) are retired by this document — permitted through `additionalProperties`, but the contract names only this key and validation plus the contract together are what stop the drift. Optional: a standing finding carried forward from an earlier round references the prior aggregate record, not this round's judge payloads, and may have no member ids to name.

file.description: Repo-relative path the cluster is anchored to, when its members share one.

line.description: 1-indexed line within `file`. Optional; an explicit `null` is also valid for a cluster whose scope is the whole file or the whole commit. `minimum` applies only when the value is a number.

evidence.description: What a skeptic can re-run or re-read to confirm the defect — drawn from the members' evidence, not invented.

alternative.description: A concrete alternative, when one member carried it. Optional at every severity.

prior_disposition.description: How this same locus was already ruled on in an EARLIER fix-loop round — set by synthesize when its inputs identify a cluster as a re-occurrence or when it carries a standing finding forward (the standing-set rule: a re-review payload spans the standing set, not the delta). Sub-fields per findings@5's declaration; every one optional.

round.description: The fix-loop round the ruling was made in, 0-based.

ruling.description: What was decided: `accepted`, `corrected-to-<severity>`, `rejected`, or `deferred` (which `follow_up_issue` must then name).

follow_up_issue.description: The issue id the deferred work was filed as.
